segments: of the Greeks? {OCR?}) Again the Tatars went forth,
and took plunder in various places,
and returned to Persia.
And when Sultan 'Ala al-Din saw that he could not withstand their army,
he imposed tribute upon himself,
and made peace with them.
And when this Sultan 'Ala al-Din was relieved of the concern of the Tatars,
he took Khilat from al-Ashraf,
and he also took many fortresses of Armenia, along with the city of Surmari.
And al-Kamil, the lord of Egypt, took Amid from its lord,
and gave him villages {OCR?} for his maintenance.
And in the year six hundred and thirty of the Arabs died the physician Muhadhdhab,
who was called al-Dakhwar,
the Damascene.
In the beginning, this man used to sit in the marketplace,
and heal the sick for a wage.
Afterwards he entered the service of one of the sons of al-'Adil,
and did much harm to the physicians, his colleagues,
and removed them from service.
For he was deceitful with his tongue and insulting,
and in his deeds profligate and shameless.
And at the end of his days, an evil disease developed in his tongue,
that with which he used to wound his companions,
and his speech was seized, and he became mute.
And that disease worsened and grew stronger upon him until it killed him with death.
And because he had no heir, he made a will,
and commanded that his courtyard should become a school for those who learn and study medicine;
and all his books as well he placed there.
And out of his wickedness he stipulated
that except for Muslims, no other person, either of the Jews or of the Christians, should enter there to study.
And this rule {OCR?} has been kept until this day in Damascus,
and students of medicine from among the Jews and the Christians study and learn outside of that school.
And in this year,
that is to say, in the ninth month of the year six hundred and thirty of the Arabs,
died Muzaffar {OCR?} al-Din Gokburi, the son of Zayn al-Din 'Ali Kuchuk {OCR?}, the lord of Arbela;
and he was conveyed to the city of Mecca,
and was buried there.
And the Caliph sent armies to Arbela with Tahir al-Din Abu 'Ali, the 'Arid al-Jaysh {OCR?},
and the commander of the army Baha' al-Din Bungush.
And when the people of Arbela were not willing to surrender,
Sharaf al-Din Sharabi was sent,
and he fought against it;
